inputs.original_text:
Listen, what we are seeing in South Dakota right now under Governor Larry Rhoden is just another textbook voter suppression tactic designed to disenfranchise vulnerable communities and strip away fundamental democratic rights. By signing Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, they are erecting deliberate bureaucratic barriers that disproportionately target marginalized groups, new registrants, and working-class people who are just trying to make their voices heard in state elections. 

They try to hide behind bureaucratic double-speak in their press release, claiming it "only appl[y] to state elections and only impacts new registrants," but make no mistake: this is part of a systemic, historical effort to restrict access to the ballot box and protect entrenched power structures at the expense of ordinary citizens. Instead of investing in our communities and removing barriers to civic participation, the establishment chooses to manufacture crises and weaponize the state apparatus to silence working people. We need urgent institutional reform to stop these relentless assaults on our democracy and to guarantee that every single person has an unhindered right to vote.
inputs.modified_text:
Let's be completely clear about what is happening right now in South Dakota under Governor Larry Rhoden: we are witnessing a deliberate, systemic assault on our democracy designed to entrench power and silence working-class people. When they signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, they put up bureaucratic barriers that specifically target vulnerable communities, marginalized groups, and new registrants. 

They try to brush this aside with bureaucratic double-speak in their press release, claiming it "only appl[y] to state elections and only impacts new registrants," but we see right through it. This is part of a historical, calculated effort to restrict access to the ballot box and protect the ruling establishment at the expense of ordinary citizens. Instead of supporting our communities and expanding civic participation, they are weaponizing the state apparatus. We desperately need urgent institutional reform to dismantle these barriers and protect the fundamental rights of working people.
